summary.text: The strongest convergent signal in ulcerative colitis mucosa is the neutrophil chemokine axis. CXCR2 leads the convergence ranking: it is up in all eight cohorts (meta log2FC [gene=CXCR2; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=2.814]), has strong Open Targets genetic association ([gene=CXCR2; type=open_targets_association; source=Open Targets Platform; genetic_association=0.8171]) and has clinical-stage antagonists in other indications. But neutrophils make almost all of its transcripts in inflamed mucosa (share [gene=CXCR2; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.965]), and only a small change survives composition adjustment ([gene=CXCR2; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=0.4409]). CXCR2 is therefore a druggable but unapproved neutrophil-recruitment target, and a strong marker of neutrophil influx rather than of a tissue programme.

Behind the neutrophil signal, several changes come from resident cells and survive composition adjustment. Epithelial DUOX2 keeps most of its rise ([gene=DUOX2; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=1.3161]), as do fibroblast MMP1 ([gene=MMP1; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=1.2636]) and myeloid IDO1 ([gene=IDO1; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=0.8505]). The epithelium also loses its metabolic programme: HMGCS2 falls in all eight cohorts (pooled [gene=HMGCS2; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=-3.838]), and its protein is lost in an independent proteomics study ([gene=HMGCS2; type=proteomics_de; source=DATASET:PROTEOMICS_SCHNIERS2019; contrast=inflamed UC at diagnosis vs healthy colon mucosa; log2_ratio=-3.094]). These are the candidates that point at a cell type rather than at cell influx, but none has human genetic support.

Genetics separates causes from consequences. The positive control IL12B, the p40 subunit blocked by ustekinumab, has plasma Mendelian randomisation in the risk direction (OR per SD [gene=IL12B; type=mendelian_randomization; source=DATASET:MR_UKBPPP_UC; odds_ratio_per_sd=1.539]), colocalising and replicating in FinnGen, which supports the design. In contrast, genetically higher plasma PD-L1 is protective (OR per SD [gene=CD274; type=mendelian_randomization; source=DATASET:MR_UKBPPP_UC; odds_ratio_per_sd=0.595]) although CD274 rises in mucosa, so PD-L1 inhibition would be the wrong direction. CXCL5 shows the same conflict, while CXCL8 has a null plasma MR (p [gene=CXCL8; type=mendelian_randomization; source=DATASET:MR_UKBPPP_UC; p=0.289]) despite one of the largest expression changes. CXCR2 has no cis instrument and could not be tested.

Baseline biopsies do not yet give drug-specific response markers. Higher CXCR2 goes with ustekinumab non-response (BH padj [gene=CXCR2; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=9.69e-6]), but the same association appears in UNIFI placebo (padj [gene=CXCR2; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.0126]). OSM, TREM1, IL11 and TNFa pathway activity follow the same pattern, so they mark disease severity rather than resistance to one drug. The drug targets IL23A and ITGB7 do not stratify response to their own drugs.

Among first-in-class candidates without a drug, the fibroblast-derived CHRDL2 and the epithelial XKR9 are the leading hypotheses for experimental validation. Both lack genetic and functional evidence: CHRDL2 is largely a fibroblast-expansion signal, and XKR9, the only intrinsic candidate, is up in only a minority of cohorts.

expression.text: The meta-analysis across eight cohorts gives a consistent picture of inflamed UC mucosa. The largest and most reproducible increases are antimicrobial, neutrophil and tissue-injury genes, each up in all eight cohorts: CHI3L1 (pooled log2FC [gene=CHI3L1; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=4.875]), MMP3 ([gene=MMP3; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=4.901]), the calprotectin subunit S100A8 ([gene=S100A8; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=4.77]), the epithelial oxidase DUOX2 ([gene=DUOX2; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=4.412]), the neutrophil chemokine CXCL8 ([gene=CXCL8; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=3.864]) and the interferon-induced IDO1 ([gene=IDO1; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=3.118]). MMP1 ([gene=MMP1; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=3.631]), MMP7 and MMP10 follow MMP3, and S100A9 follows S100A8. Together they describe a mucosa filled with neutrophils and myeloid cells, remodelling its matrix and producing reactive oxygen and antimicrobial proteins.

The decreases are just as strong and point to loss of differentiated colonocyte function. AQP8 shows the largest pooled decrease ([gene=AQP8; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=-5.246]), and the ketogenesis enzyme HMGCS2 is down in all eight cohorts ([gene=HMGCS2; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=-3.838]). The chloride/bicarbonate exchanger SLC26A3, a UC genetic locus, is also down ([gene=SLC26A3; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=-1.702]). CLDN8, SLC26A2 and ADH1C belong to the same lost absorptive and metabolic programme. These genes are good activity biomarkers; for SLC26A3, restoration rather than inhibition would be the therapeutic logic if it were causal.

Several highly ranked genes owe their rank to genetics and tractability rather than to the size of their expression change. JAK2 rises only modestly though consistently (pooled [gene=JAK2; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=0.874]), and CD274 (PD-L1) shows a moderate increase ([gene=CD274; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=1.974]) that most likely reflects interferon-driven induction and immune-cell influx. The direction of the top changes is consistent across cohorts, but their size is not: heterogeneity is high, driven by platform differences and compressed microarray fold changes.

inflammation.text: Comparing inflamed with non-inflamed mucosa from the same patients shows that the neutrophil signal is local. CXCR2 is clearly higher in inflamed than in paired non-inflamed tissue (log2FC [gene=CXCR2; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed_vs_noninflamed_paired; log2fc=1.6972]), and the change holds after adjustment for segment, age and sex. It therefore marks active inflammation in the biopsy rather than a constitutive trait of UC mucosa.

Its partner receptor CXCR1 shows an even larger local change between paired inflamed and non-inflamed tissue (log2FC [gene=CXCR1; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed_vs_noninflamed_paired; log2fc=2.193]), consistent with the same neutrophil influx.

The epithelial metabolic loss is also confined to inflamed tissue. HMGCS2 is not changed in non-inflamed UC mucosa versus controls (padj [gene=HMGCS2; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=noninflamed_vs_control; padj=0.675]) but falls sharply between paired non-inflamed and inflamed tissue (log2FC [gene=HMGCS2; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed_vs_noninflamed_paired; log2fc=-1.9508]). It reports local injury rather than a field defect present before inflammation, and the change survives adjustment for segment, age and sex.

CHI3L1 has one of the strongest local components (paired log2FC [gene=CHI3L1; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed_vs_noninflamed_paired; log2fc=2.6182]), whereas JAK2 changes only slightly between paired inflamed and non-inflamed tissue ([gene=JAK2; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed_vs_noninflamed_paired; log2fc=0.4031]), in keeping with JAK2 acting through signalling rather than transcript abundance.

replication.text: Replication is the strongest feature of the leading genes. CXCR2, CXCL8, IDO1, CHI3L1, MMP3, DUOX2, S100A8 and HMGCS2 change in the same direction in the discovery cohort and in all four microarray and three RNA-seq replication cohorts, and CXCL8 holds after adjustment for colon segment, age and sex ([gene=CXCL8; type=expression_adjusted; source=DATASET:GSE193677; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed UC vs control, biopsy level; adjusted_log2fc=2.499]); CXCR1 replicates in most but not all cohorts. At protein level, the independent proteomics study confirms the loss of HMGCS2 and the rise of S100A8 ([gene=S100A8; type=proteomics_de; source=DATASET:PROTEOMICS_SCHNIERS2019; contrast=inflamed UC at diagnosis vs healthy colon mucosa; log2_ratio=2.749]), DUOX2 ([gene=DUOX2; type=proteomics_de; source=DATASET:PROTEOMICS_SCHNIERS2019; contrast=inflamed UC at diagnosis vs healthy colon mucosa; log2_ratio=1.468]) and IDO1 ([gene=IDO1; type=proteomics_de; source=DATASET:PROTEOMICS_SCHNIERS2019; contrast=inflamed UC at diagnosis vs healthy colon mucosa; log2_ratio=0.917]). The CHI3L1 protein rise is much smaller than its RNA change ([gene=CHI3L1; type=proteomics_de; source=DATASET:PROTEOMICS_SCHNIERS2019; contrast=inflamed UC at diagnosis vs healthy colon mucosa; log2_ratio=0.607]) and was not called significant by the study authors. Proteomics covers only a subset of genes, and an unmeasured gene is not evidence against it.

literature.text: Published support is thinnest where the convergence score is highest. CXCR2 has no verbatim-checked literature relation in the graph. Its corpus support is indirect: abstracts naming CXCR1 and CXCR2 as neutrophil extracellular trap-related treatment targets in UC on Mendelian randomisation and transcriptomic grounds, a CXCL5/CXCR2 axis study integrating eQTL, pQTL and transcriptome data, and machine-extracted PubTator3 associations. No UC trial of a CXCR2 antagonist appears in the corpus. For CXCL8, the literature places the CXCL8-CXCR1/CXCR2 axis upstream of PI3K/Akt, MAPK and NF-kappaB signalling, names it a protein-interaction hub, and reports it as a blood diagnostic gene for IBD as a whole, which is review-level or bioinformatic support.

Mechanistic literature exists for a few other leading genes but comes from single studies. IDO1 was elevated in UC and drove M1 macrophage polarisation through the GRP78-XBP1 stress pathway, and an IDO inhibitor ameliorated DSS colitis. AQP9, predominantly neutrophilic, promoted neutrophil extracellular trap formation through JAK2-STAT3-mediated pyroptosis in mouse colitis, which again places the AQP9 signal in infiltrating neutrophils. CHI3L1 promoted macrophage pyroptosis through a BCAT1/NF-kappaB axis, and velpatasvir bound recombinant CHI3L1 in vitro, a repurposing lead only.

Most gene-level literature is diagnostic or bioinformatic. MMP1 correlated with endoscopic and histological indices among transcripts modified by mirikizumab, and was proposed as a diagnostic marker in UC-associated cancer. DUOX2 protein is among the most elevated in inflamed biopsies, and inhibiting its overexpression alleviated colitis in one herbal-formula study. MMP10 was up in active versus remitting UC and before diagnosis, S100A9 performed well for active UC and fell in resident macrophages with tofacitinib response, CXCL1 appeared in several diagnostic models, and down-regulated SLC26A2 tracked Mayo score and PUCAI. These are mostly single-study or in-silico results with few prospective validations.

external.text: Approved UC target classes behave as positive controls. IL12B, the p40 subunit targeted by ustekinumab, has a plasma MR in the risk direction (OR per SD [gene=IL12B; type=mendelian_randomization; source=DATASET:MR_UKBPPP_UC; odds_ratio_per_sd=1.539]) that colocalises with the IBD GWAS signal and replicates in FinnGen, so genetics supports inhibition; its instruments are heterogeneous and the signal is shared with psoriasis. JAK2 has a high Open Targets association (score [gene=JAK2; type=open_targets_association; source=Open Targets Platform; score=0.7318]) but only a small expression change and no MR instrument. The expression-led candidates have no approved UC drug. CXCR2 has an Open Targets overall association of [gene=CXCR2; type=open_targets_association; source=Open Targets Platform; score=0.5345] and antagonists from other indications (reparixin at phase 3; navarixin, ladarixin, danirixin and SX-682 at phase 2). It is not strongly constrained, has no curated safety events and lacks a cis-pQTL or gut eQTL instrument, which is not evidence against it. Mouse literature reports a CXCR2 antagonist ameliorating acute colitis, but MGI has no curated colitis phenotype for it or for the other genes checked.

Mendelian randomisation exposes direction conflicts. Genetically higher plasma PD-L1 lowers UC risk (OR per SD [gene=CD274; type=mendelian_randomization; source=DATASET:MR_UKBPPP_UC; odds_ratio_per_sd=0.595]); the signal colocalises with an IBD GWAS signal and replicates in FinnGen (OR [gene=CD274; type=mendelian_randomization; source=DATASET:MR_UKBPPP_UC; finngen_odds_ratio_per_sd=0.734]), with nominal heterogeneity across its three instruments (p [gene=CD274; type=mr_sensitivity; source=DATASET:MR_UKBPPP_UC; layer=plasma_protein; heterogeneity_p=0.0259]). The mucosal rise of CD274 is therefore probably protective feedback. CXCL5 is likewise up in biopsies but genetically protective (OR per SD [gene=CXCL5; type=mendelian_randomization; source=DATASET:MR_UKBPPP_UC; odds_ratio_per_sd=0.634]); it replicates in FinnGen but does not colocalise, so a neighbouring variant cannot be excluded. The plasma MR is null for CXCL8, IDO1 (p [gene=IDO1; type=mendelian_randomization; source=DATASET:MR_UKBPPP_UC; p=0.111]) and FCGR2A (p [gene=FCGR2A; type=mendelian_randomization; source=DATASET:MR_UKBPPP_UC; p=0.68]), and the IDO1 colon eQTL and the FCGR2A gut single-cell eQTL are also not significant. MMP1 and the other MMPs have no Open Targets genetic association and only broad MMP inhibitors exist.

Gut-tissue MR adds loci that the blood layer does not test. In OLFM4+ crypt progenitors, genetically higher SLC26A3 expression gives an odds ratio above one (OR per SD [gene=SLC26A3; type=mendelian_randomization_gut; source=DATASET:MR_GUT_EQTL_UC; layer=gut_cell; odds_ratio_per_sd=1.607]), colocalising and replicating in FinnGen; this conflicts with its loss in inflamed biopsies, which is therefore more likely a consequence of inflammation, and it rests on one instrument in one cell type. In transverse colon, IRF8 (OR per SD [gene=IRF8; type=mendelian_randomization_gut; source=DATASET:MR_GUT_EQTL_UC; layer=colon_tissue; odds_ratio_per_sd=1.937]) and IRF5 expression raise UC risk with colocalisation, as genetically supported but non-biopsy-led candidates. Blood and gut layers rarely test the same genes, so their agreement cannot be judged for the leading candidates.

cells.text: The single-cell data split the leading genes into markers of neutrophil influx and changes within resident cells. Neutrophils make most of the inflamed-mucosa transcripts of CXCR2 (share [gene=CXCR2; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.965]), CXCL8 ([gene=CXCL8; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.873]) and S100A8 ([gene=S100A8; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.909]), and AQP9 follows the same pattern. After composition adjustment CXCL8 is no longer significant (padj [gene=CXCL8; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_padj=0.0523]), and CXCR2 keeps only a small change (adjusted [gene=CXCR2; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=0.4409]), as do AQP9 ([gene=AQP9; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=0.8551]) and S100A8 ([gene=S100A8; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=0.9231]). These are markers of neutrophil recruitment, and targeting CXCR2 means blocking neutrophil arrival rather than correcting a tissue programme. The CXCR2 attribution does not replicate: Smillie 2019 has no neutrophils and assigns it to a few T/NK and macrophage cells, and the second dataset points to myeloid cells. CXCL8 comes from macrophages in Smillie, replicated, so its source is myeloid as well as neutrophil.

Other leading genes are made by resident cells and keep a large change after adjustment. DUOX2 is epithelial (lineage share [gene=DUOX2; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; dominant_lineage_share=0.947]), replicated in the second dataset, and keeps most of its rise ([gene=DUOX2; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=1.3161]). MMP1 comes from inflammatory fibroblasts, replicated, with little neutrophil contribution, and keeps a large adjusted change ([gene=MMP1; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=1.2636]). IDO1 comes from DC1 and macrophages, replicated, with enterocytes contributing in Gubatan, and stays significant after adjustment ([gene=IDO1; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=0.8505]). These are the candidates with a defined producing cell: epithelial DUOX2, fibroblast MMP1 and myeloid IDO1.

CD274 sits in between: neutrophil states carry much of it in Gubatan ([gene=CD274; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.687]), Smillie spreads it diffusely over plasma cells, macrophages and enterocytes, and a significant change remains after adjustment ([gene=CD274; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=0.4978]).

LCN2 shows the over-correction caveat of the adjustment. It is made by epithelial cells (transit-amplifying cells and enterocytes, replicated, with a low neutrophil share), yet its bulk rise is no longer significant after adjustment (padj [gene=LCN2; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_padj=0.206]). Because lineage scores move with epithelial loss and resident-cell activation, a lost signal is not proof of pure influx, while a retained one is strong evidence of a tissue change. LCN2 is best treated as a marker, not a proven target.

spatial.text: In-situ evidence is available only for MMP1. In the deconvolved Visium spots, inflammatory fibroblasts explain most of its signal (contribution [gene=MMP1; type=spatial_visium_cell; source=DATASET:GSE189184; in_situ_contribution=0.579]), with neutrophils as a minor contributor and neighbour of its high spots, which agrees with the single-cell attribution to inflammatory fibroblasts. MMP1 is not on the Xenium panel and CosMx detects it only at background, so the tissue-level and single-cell spatial views do not yet agree and the attribution lacks in-situ confirmation at single-cell resolution. The other leading candidates were not examined spatially.

pathways.text: Inflamed mucosa activates nearly every inflammatory pathway at once. JAK-STAT activity is raised in all eight cohorts with none decreased, strongest in GSE193677 (t [type=pathway_activity; source=ANALYSIS:pathways; per_cohort.GSE193677.t=15.68]), and inferred STAT3 activity is also up in all eight cohorts (GSE193677 t [type=tf_activity; source=ANALYSIS:pathways; per_cohort.GSE193677.t=20.6]). TNFa and NF-kB are up in all eight cohorts (TNFa in GSE206285 t [type=pathway_activity; source=ANALYSIS:pathways; per_cohort.GSE206285.t=20.07]), as are EGFR, hypoxia, TGFb, MAPK and PI3K. The TNF and JAK-STAT axes are therefore active and already drug-targeted, but this broad activation is shared by all inflamed samples and does not discriminate between candidates. Not every pathway rises: androgen activity does not replicate, being up in some cohorts and down in others (GSE109142 t [type=pathway_activity; source=ANALYSIS:pathways; per_cohort.GSE109142.t=-10.8]), and p53 is down in a minority of cohorts and up in none.

The most specific cell-cell circuit is neutrophil-to-neutrophil. The CXCR4-high neutrophil state sends CXCL8 to CXCR2 on the generic neutrophil state, with a large rise over uninflamed tissue (log2 change [type=cell_communication; source=ANALYSIS:communication; log2_change=2.755]), a feed-forward recruitment loop. Neutrophil CXCL8 also pairs with ACKR1 on venular endothelium, the highest-scoring CXCL8 pair (score [type=cell_communication; source=ANALYSIS:communication; score_inflamed=7870.993]); because ACKR1 is an atypical receptor, this is chemokine presentation and leukocyte trafficking rather than classical signalling. IL1B from monocyte-derived macrophages and neutrophil states pairs with IL1R2 on neutrophil states (log2 change at the CXCR4-high receiver [type=cell_communication; source=ANALYSIS:communication; log2_change=2.059]); IL1R2 is mostly a decoy receptor, so this pair may be a brake as much as a driver. These scores are co-expression in one single-cell dataset, not proof of signalling.

Separating targeted from untargeted axes: TNF, JAK-STAT and IL-23 are already treated in UC. The CXCL8-CXCR1/CXCR2 circuit is druggable, with CXCR2 antagonists that reached phase 2 or phase 3 in other indications, but untargeted in UC. TREM1, up in all eight cohorts, has only the phase 2 peptide nangibotide, and no ligand-receptor circuit could be assigned to it in this dataset. IL-1 is targeted in other diseases but not in UC. Neutrophil-directed antagonists carry an infection risk that was not assessed here.

treatment.text: Baseline pathway activity tracks severity rather than resistance to a specific drug. TNFa activity is higher in ustekinumab non-responders (BH padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.0000484]) but also in UNIFI placebo non-responders (padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.00608]), while the small PURSUIT placebo arm shows nothing (padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (PURSUIT).padj=0.932]). NF-kB activity is higher in non-responders to most drugs and in UNIFI placebo, but not in the mesalamine or etrolizumab arms. TGFb is associated with ustekinumab non-response (padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.000493]) and UNIFI placebo, but not with golimumab (padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.golimumab.padj=0.348]). JAK-STAT goes with ustekinumab non-response (padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.0124]) but not vedolizumab (padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.vedolizumab.padj=0.571]), and placebo is borderline, so its specificity is unproven. Pathway-level drug-vs-placebo interactions were not tested.

At gene level the pattern is the same. OSM is higher in ustekinumab non-responders (padj [gene=OSM; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.0000264]), but the drug-vs-placebo interaction is null (padj [gene=OSM; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; interaction.ustekinumab.padj=0.982]) and the placebo trend runs the same way (padj [gene=OSM; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.116]). IL11 has the strongest ustekinumab association among the genes checked (padj [gene=IL11; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=3.68e-8]) but is also higher in placebo non-responders (padj [gene=IL11; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.0133]). TREM1 (ustekinumab padj [gene=TREM1; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.0000474]; placebo padj [gene=TREM1; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.0234]) and CXCR2 likewise mark severity, and CXCR2 is not associated with golimumab response (padj [gene=CXCR2; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.golimumab.padj=0.994]). In the adalimumab single-cell atlas, CXCL8 shows no baseline difference and falls after treatment in cycling mononuclear phagocytes (padj [gene=CXCL8; type=antitnf_singlecell; source=DATASET:GSE282122; after_vs_before_treatment.1.padj=0.0253]) in a small cohort. The drugs' own targets do not stratify response: baseline IL23A for ustekinumab (padj [gene=IL23A; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.977]) and ITGB7 for vedolizumab (padj [gene=ITGB7; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.vedolizumab.padj=0.995]). Response cohorts outside UNIFI are small, so null results partly reflect low power.

discovery.text: CHRDL2 is the top first-in-class candidate from the discovery screen. It is antibody-tractable with no clinical drug, and its transcripts come mostly from inflammatory fibroblasts. Only a minority of its bulk signal is retained after composition correction (retained [gene=CHRDL2; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; retained=0.2764]), so much of it reflects fibroblast expansion. Its vital-organ RNA reaches [gene=CHRDL2; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; vital_max_ntpm=42.6] nTPM, the highest of the group, which is a safety point to check. Genetic and functional evidence is missing. It is a hypothesis for testing whether fibroblast-derived CHRDL2 modulates BMP signalling in inflamed mucosa.

XKR9 is the only leading novel candidate classed as intrinsic: it is epithelial, and most of its change survives composition correction (retained [gene=XKR9; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; retained=0.7976]). But it is up in only [gene=XKR9; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; cohorts_up=4] cohorts and few cells express it, so its replication is weaker than that of the convergence leaders. Validation would need protein detection in epithelium and replication in further cohorts before any tractability work.

CPXM1 is a stromal fibroblast candidate whose cell attribution replicates in a second single-cell dataset. Less than half of its change is retained after adjustment ([gene=CPXM1; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; retained=0.4136]), so it is partly a fibroblast-expansion signal. Its vital-organ expression is low, but there is no genetic or functional evidence for it in UC.

LAX1 is a negative result of the screen. It is made mainly by plasma and T cells, its lineage does not replicate in the second dataset, and only a small share survives composition correction (retained [gene=LAX1; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; retained=0.2300]). It most likely reflects lymphocyte infiltration rather than a tissue change and is not a first-in-class target.

integration.text: The streams agree on the neutrophil axis and on the approved positive controls. CXCR2 converges across expression, replication, paired inflammation, Open Targets genetics and tractability, and the pathway stream finds the CXCL8-CXCR2 neutrophil circuit to be the most specific cell-cell signal. The IL12B positive control is supported by plasma MR and Open Targets, and the JAK-STAT and TNF pathways are active in all cohorts, consistent with the approved drug classes. Expression, paired analysis and proteomics agree that HMGCS2 and the absorptive epithelial programme are lost locally in inflamed tissue.

The streams disagree in three places. First, the cell and treatment streams downgrade the top of the ranking: the CXCR2 and CXCL8 bulk signals are largely neutrophil influx, and their association with poor response is mirrored in placebo, so they mark severity. Second, genetics contradicts expression for CD274 and CXCL5, both up in mucosa but genetically protective, and for SLC26A3, lost in mucosa but with a risk-direction gut eQTL; the CXCL8 MR is null despite one of the largest expression changes. Third, the tissue-intrinsic candidates with a clear producing cell (DUOX2, MMP1, IDO1) lack genetic support, while the genetically supported JAK2 and the gut-eQTL loci IRF5 and IRF8 barely move in expression. The literature stream is thin for the top genes, with no verbatim-checked relations for CXCR2 or CD274.

targets.rationale: Ranks first on convergence: up in all eight cohorts and locally in inflamed mucosa, with strong Open Targets genetic association and clinical-stage antagonists in other indications. Kept first, but as a neutrophil-recruitment target rather than a tissue target: neutrophils make most of its transcripts, little change survives composition adjustment, no MR instrument exists, and its link to poor ustekinumab response is mirrored in placebo, so it also marks severity.

Positive control: the approved ustekinumab target has plasma MR in the risk direction, colocalisation with the IBD GWAS signal and FinnGen replication. Placed above the expression-led genes because it has causal genetic support, although it is not in the top of the expression ranking.

Positive control for the approved JAK-inhibitor class: high Open Targets association and JAK-STAT and STAT3 activity up in every cohort, despite only a modest mRNA change. Its rank comes from genetics and tractability, not from expression, and it has no MR instrument.

The best-supported tissue-intrinsic candidate: strongly up in all eight cohorts, made by inflammatory fibroblasts in two single-cell datasets and in deconvolved Visium spots, and keeps a large change after composition adjustment. Held below the positive controls because it lacks genetic support and only broad MMP inhibitors exist.

Epithelial oxidase up in all eight cohorts, confirmed at protein level, replicated as epithelial in two single-cell datasets and largely retained after composition adjustment. An intrinsic epithelial activation signal and activity biomarker; it has no genetic support or clinical drug.

Up in all eight cohorts and at protein level, made by myeloid cells and retained after adjustment, and inhibitors exist from oncology. Classed as a biomarker rather than a target because plasma and colon MR are null and it is probably an interferon-induced counter-regulatory gene, so the direction of intervention is unclear.

One of the largest and most reproducible increases and the ligand of the dominant neutrophil circuit, ranked third numerically. Moved down because its signal is lost after composition adjustment, its plasma MR is null and its association with non-response is mirrored in placebo, so it is a marker of neutrophil activity rather than a causal target.
The clearest loss of epithelial metabolism: down in all eight cohorts, at protein level and only in inflamed tissue. A local activity biomarker, not a target.

One of the largest RNA increases with a strong local component that holds after covariate adjustment, and mechanistic literature linking it to macrophage pyroptosis. The protein rise is much smaller and not significant, and there is no genetic support, so it is kept as a biomarker.
Calprotectin subunit up in all eight cohorts and at protein level, made mainly by neutrophils: a positive control for the established calprotectin activity marker rather than a target.

Ranked fourth numerically but placed low: it rises in mucosa, yet genetically higher plasma PD-L1 is protective, with colocalisation and FinnGen replication. Inhibition would be the wrong direction; the mucosal rise is best read as protective feedback and a marker of interferon-driven inflammation.

Myeloid receptor up in all eight cohorts with a phase 2 peptide antagonist, but no ligand-receptor circuit was assigned and its association with ustekinumab non-response is mirrored in placebo, so it also marks severity.

Exploratory: the top first-in-class candidate of the discovery screen, antibody-tractable and fibroblast-derived, but largely a fibroblast-expansion signal with relatively high vital-organ RNA and no genetic or functional evidence.

Exploratory: the only intrinsic epithelial candidate of the discovery screen, with most of its change retained after composition correction, but up in only a minority of cohorts and expressed in few cells.

limitations.text: The convergence score rewards neutrophil-driven genes because bulk expression mixes cell influx with tissue change; the composition adjustment corrects for this but can over-correct when resident cells activate.

Mendelian randomisation covers only genes with a cis-pQTL or gut eQTL instrument; CXCR2 and most leading candidates could not be tested, and absence of a test is not evidence against causality. Plasma protein is not mucosal protein.
Paired and covariate-adjusted analyses come from one cohort (MSCCR), proteomics from one small study, and ligand-receptor circuits from one single-cell dataset; Smillie 2019 lacks neutrophils.
Treatment-response cohorts outside UNIFI are small, and pathway-level drug-vs-placebo interactions were not tested, so null results partly reflect low power.
Spatial evidence exists only for MMP1, and the downregulated epithelial genes were not examined at single-cell level.
Literature support for the leading genes is mostly bioinformatic or single preclinical studies; CXCR2, CD274, FCGR2A, JAK2 and TREM1 have no verbatim-checked literature relation in the corpus.
